AddressComponents.description: The parts of an address's label. Each is null when the filing did not carry it.

line1.description: The number, directions, street name and suffix: `1200 Quillfeather Ln`.

AddressKind.description: The `type` of everything about an address: always `address`.

AddressListing.description:
How an address is listed on a business: `principal` and `mailing` are the addresses
the business filed as such; `registered_office` is its registered agent's office and
`officer` an officer's address, each either filed or reached only through the agent or
the officer (so the business did not file it itself). The set is open: a client treats
a value it does not know as `other`.

businesses.description:
The businesses filed at the address, the ones filed as their principal or
mailing address first: each item carries `listed_as`, how the business filed it,
and never `role`; each item's `token` is a `business_token` `POST /searches`
redeems, pinned to this address. `count` is every business.

people.description:
The people who filed from the address, best known first, leaving out a
registered agent's company. A person is at an address with no role of its own
there, so an item carries no role key. `count` is everyone who serves a business.

label.description:
The address as one line, rendered verbatim: the street, then the city, state
and ZIP.

token.description:
Opaque handle for the address, sealed like a business's and bound to the same
organization and fifteen minutes. Nothing redeems one yet: pick one of the
address's businesses instead.

AddressesResponse.description:
`GET /autocomplete/addresses`: the addresses typed text fits, most businesses first,
each with the businesses filed there. A pick is one of those businesses.

found.description: Addresses matched before `limit`; a floor when `found_capped`.

found_capped.description: `found` is a floor rather than an exact count.

truncated.description: The search did not finish, so an address that fits may be missing.

BusinessKind.description:
The `type` of everything about a business, a suggestion or a related item: always
`business`. A client tells the three kinds of entity apart by this key alone.

BusinessRelated.description:
What a business is related to: the people who hold a role on it and the addresses it
filed.

matched_name.description:
A name the business is also known by that fits the typed name better than `label` does,
when there is one; null when `label` fits at least as well.

oneOf.description:
The legal structure the domicile registration is filed under, unformatted;
null when it is not known.

token.description:
Opaque handle for the family: pass it back verbatim as `business_token` on
`POST /searches` to pre-identify the business the search resolves to.
Sealed by the autocomplete service, so a client cannot read the id inside, and the same
family gets a different token every time. Bound to the session's
organization and good for fifteen minutes; `POST /searches` refuses it
from another organization (422, code 3040) or past its expiry (422, code
3042).

found_capped.description:
`found` is a floor rather than an exact count — it hit the disclosure
threshold, or the scan stopped once the head was provably settled.

This says nothing about whether the SUGGESTIONS are complete; read
`truncated` for that. The two were one flag, and a caller could not tell
"there are more than this many" from "I did not finish looking".

truncated.description:
The search did not finish: a deadline fired or a scan budget was spent, so
a business that matches may be missing from `suggestions` entirely.

The distinction that matters to a client is that `found: 0` with this set
is NOT evidence of absence — it means the autocomplete service stopped looking, usually
because the pages it needed were cold. Rendered as a count ("0 matches")
it tells the caller their business does not exist, which is a lie the UI
used to tell. A complete answer, however few rows it has, leaves it false.

ErrorEnvelope.description:
The error envelope the API answers with: a numeric `code`, a `message`, and
`metadata` that names the reason.

MatchGrade.description:
How the best of a business's names fits the typed name: `exact` is the name itself,
`strong` starts with it or has it at a later word, and `partial` has every word of it,
in another order or spread over the business's names. The set is open: a client treats
a value it does not know as `partial`.

PeopleResponse.description:
`GET /autocomplete/people`: the people a typed name fits, best first, each with
the businesses they hold a role on. A pick is one of those businesses.

found.description: People matched before `limit`; a floor when `found_capped`.

found_capped.description: `found` is a floor rather than an exact count.

truncated.description: The search did not finish, so a person who fits may be missing.

PersonKind.description: The `type` of everything about a person: always `person`.

addresses.description:
The addresses the person filed from. A person is at an address with no role of its
own there, so an item carries no role key.

businesses.description:
The businesses the person holds a role on: each item carries `role`, the role
the person holds there, and never `listed_as`; each item's `token` is a
`business_token` `POST /searches` redeems, reached through this person.

PersonRole.description:
The role a person holds on a business, as the index's `people_roles.role` has it:
`officer` or `agent` (the registered agent). The set is open: a client treats a value it does not know as `other`.

states.description:
The states of the businesses the person holds a role on, listed as a business
suggestion's `states` is.

token.description:
Opaque handle for the person, sealed like a business's and bound to the same
organization and fifteen minutes. Nothing redeems one yet: pick one of the
person's businesses instead.

RelatedAddress.description: An address listed under a business or under a person.

highlight.description:
How this address reads against the typed text of the address filter, drawn as a
suggestion's own `highlight` is; null on an address no filter matched, and on a
matched one whose highlight marks nothing.

listed_as.description:
How this address is on the business, on an address listed under a business; see
`AddressListing` for `officer` and `registered_office`, which also cover an address reached only
through the business's officers or registered agent. Absent under a person: a
person is at an address with no role of its own there, and absent where the filing
names none.

matched.description: This item is why the row is here.

RelatedAddresses.description: The addresses related to a business or a person.

count.description:
Total before the head cap; null when the relation's status is not ok. For
the addresses of a business it counts the business's own filings: the head
also ranks in the addresses of its officers and agents, so `items` can
outnumber it.

matched.description: How many satisfied a relation filter; null when none applies.

RelatedBusiness.description: A business listed under a person (`role`) or under an address (`listed_as`).

address.description:
The lead address, the one the business's own row leads with; null when the family
has none.

highlight.description:
How the name this item matched on (`matched_name` when that is it, else `label`)
reads against the typed text of the business name filter, drawn as a suggestion's
own `highlight` is. An item with a `matched_name` always carries an array, which
may mark nothing where the name matched in a way no word of it shows; otherwise it
is null on an item no filter matched, and on a matched item whose highlight marks
nothing.

listed_as.description:
How the address is on this business, on a business listed under an address; see
`AddressListing` for `officer` and `registered_office`, which also cover an address reached only
through the business's officers or registered agent. Absent elsewhere, and where
the filing names none.

matched.description: This item is why the row is here.

matched_name.description:
Another of the business's names that fits the business name filtering the answer
better than `label` does, as a business suggestion's `matched_name` means it; null
when `label` fits at least as well or no business name filters.

role.description:
The role the related person holds on this business, on a business listed under a
person. Absent elsewhere, and where the filing names none.

states.description: The states, listed as the business's own row lists them.

token.description:
Opaque handle for this business, sealed the way a suggestion's own `token` is and
bound to the same organization and fifteen minutes: a `business_token` that
`POST /searches` redeems, pinned to the row it was reached through.

RelatedBusinesses.description: The businesses related to a person or an address.

count.description:
Total before the head cap; null when the relation's status is not ok. For
the addresses of a business it counts the business's own filings: the head
also ranks in the addresses of its officers and agents, so `items` can
outnumber it.

matched.description: How many satisfied a relation filter; null when none applies.

RelatedItem.description:
A related item of any kind, told apart by its `type`. Each relation holds one kind,
so no response field has this type; it is the union a generic client can decode any
related item as. `type` is the discriminator and is fixed by the relation, which holds
one kind, so it is not an open enum and an item of another kind in a relation is a
contract violation. A new kind of entity would arrive as a new relation, which a client
that does not know it ignores.

RelatedPeople.description: The people related to a business or an address.

count.description:
Total before the head cap; null when the relation's status is not ok. For
the addresses of a business it counts the business's own filings: the head
also ranks in the addresses of its officers and agents, so `items` can
outnumber it.

matched.description: How many satisfied a relation filter; null when none applies.

RelatedPerson.description: A person listed under a business or under an address.

highlight.description:
How the name this person matched on reads against the typed text of the person
name filter, drawn as a suggestion's own `highlight` is; null on a person no filter
matched, and on a matched one whose highlight marks nothing.

matched.description: This item is why the row is here.

role.description:
The role this person holds on the business, on a person listed under a business.
Absent under an address: a person is at an address with no role of its own there.

RouteUnservedEnvelope.description: The error envelope of a 503 for a route this replica cannot answer yet.

RouteUnservedMetadata.description:
The `metadata` of a 503 for a route this replica cannot answer yet: what it has
(`current`: the index's schema, or the token version it seals) and the least the
route needs (`required`).

RouteUnservedReason.description: Why a route this service has cannot answer on this replica yet.

SourceStatus.description:
Whether a relation was read. The set is open: a client treats a value it does not know
as `unavailable`.

ValidationErrorEnvelope.description:
The error envelope of a 422: a request whose parameters do not validate. What a
framework default answered as `{"detail": [...]}` is `metadata.errors`.

ValidationItem.description:
One parameter that failed validation. The `type` is open: a client treats one it does
not know as a generic failure.

ValidationMetadata.description: The `metadata` of a 422: the reason, and every parameter that failed.

recipe_version.description: The rules that built the content; reported, never pinned.

schema_version.description: The DDL the artifact is built on; the number this service pins.

service_version.description: `<crate version>+<commit>` of the binary that answered, e.g. `0.3.0+7c3d1ab9e`.

info.description: Keystroke typeahead over businesses, over the people who hold a role on them, and over the addresses they filed, served from the read-only SQLite index. Every request carries a session grant minted by `POST /autocomplete/sessions`.
info.title: Baselayer Autocomplete

parameters.description:
An address as it is written: every word but the last matched whole, the last as
the start of a word, accents and case ignored, and a street suffix, unit or
direction matched in every spelling USPS Publication 28 lists for it (`street`
finds `St`). Two or more characters, at most 256.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: 1–20, default 10.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Comma list of `businesses`, `people`; default `businesses`.
parameters.name: include

parameters.description: Comma list of state codes; keeps the addresses in any of them.
parameters.name: state

parameters.description:
A person's name, every word the start of a word of theirs; keeps the addresses
a person it fits filed from. At most 256 characters.
parameters.name: person.name

parameters.description:
A business name, matched as on the businesses route; keeps the addresses a
business it fits filed as its own principal or mailing address, never as its
registered agent's office. At most 256 characters.
parameters.name: business.name

200.description: Addresses, most businesses first, each with the businesses a pick is made from

401.description: Session missing, invalid or expired: mint one

403.description: The session's scope does not reach this route (code 501), or a parameter touches a relation it leaves out (code 502, `metadata.param`)

422.description: A parameter is unknown, repeated or invalid, `limit` is past the session's most, or a filter (`state`, `person.name`, `business.name`) was sent with a query too short to narrow

429.description: Rate limited, the session's request budget is spent, or the session changed its query too many times

503.description: This replica cannot answer address search yet: the served index predates it (`metadata.reason` `index_too_old`) or the autocomplete service seals tokens older than version 6 (`token_version_too_old`), with what it has as `current` and the least the route needs as `required`. A 503 with no index served yet, or with every query worker busy, carries an ErrorEnvelope instead.
